title: TE-4 — Managed Table Tools Delivery
summary: add resizable columns, Reset, and Copy as CSV to the shared Content Detail table view through Manage-owned contributions
content_html:
TE-4 — Managed Table Tools Delivery

Status And Purpose

Proposed as TE-4, after TE-3 proves the public-safe content-detail main view and lightweight static Markdown table presentation in public and Manage readers.

TE-4 adds table tools only through the Manage composition. It extends the same registered view, main-panel layout, exact table target, semantic table renderer, and main-view toolbar. It does not create a managed table viewer beside the public one.

Complete Outcome

When the active Content Detail target is a Markdown table on a Manage route, the table supports pointer and keyboard-accessible column resizing with session-local Reset widths. The existing main-view toolbar also offers Copy as CSV.

The public table view remains the static TE-3 presentation. No source, table identity, column widths, or exported file is persisted. Copy reads only the accepted semantic table presentation and emits no successful-action status message.

Current Seams And Expected Size

The likely owners are the Manage view/control contributions, shared content-detail table adapter extension points frozen by TE-3, main-view control handlers, table presentation CSS, a pure CSV serializer, clipboard adapter, and focused browser-module tests.

The indicative shape is 3–6 touched production files, approximately 250–450 production JavaScript/CSS lines and 200–350 focused test lines. TE-4.0 must record the exact shared-versus-Manage ownership, files, and separate resizing/CSV estimates. If the tools require a second view, renderer fork, source parser, stable table registry, or public module dependency on Manage code, stop before implementation.

Rough Delivery Steps

TE-4.0 — Trace And Freeze Manage Contributions

  • [ ] Trace TE-3 target/view lifecycle, semantic table structure, natural-width calculation, main-view control contributions, Manage entrypoint boundaries, and public import-graph enforcement.
  • [ ] Freeze resize handles, pointer capture, keyboard increments, minimum/maximum widths, sticky-column offset response, session lifetime, Reset, and supported desktop-width behavior.
  • [ ] Freeze CSV header inclusion, row/cell ordering, visible-text extraction, whitespace and line-break normalization, empty cells, quoting, delimiter/newline convention, link labels, and unsupported cell states.
  • [ ] Freeze explicit clipboard invocation, no-success-message behavior, failure projection, and focus preservation.
  • [ ] Record exact files, reused seams, rough production/test diffs, and any proposed expansion before implementation approval.

Checkpoint: one accepted table fixture proves resizing and Reset without breaking sticky header/column geometry, plus exact CSV output for links, commas, quotes, line breaks, empty cells, and wrapped content. Public composition contains none of the Manage tool modules or controls. Stop before implementation.

TE-4.1 — Add Resizable Columns

  • [ ] Contribute Manage-only table capability to the active shared table target without changing public target or renderer identity.
  • [ ] Add accessible component resize handles to eligible header boundaries.
  • [ ] Recompute the table and sticky first-column geometry through the focused table adapter only.
  • [ ] Add Reset widths to the existing main-view toolbar and restore the TE-3 natural-width presentation for the active session.
  • [ ] Release all resize listeners and transient widths on Back, navigation, target replacement, or view disposal.

TE-4.2 — Add Copy As CSV

  • [ ] Implement the frozen pure semantic-table-to-CSV serializer independently of Markdown source and report models.
  • [ ] Add Copy as CSV to the existing main-view toolbar only for eligible Manage table targets.
  • [ ] Request clipboard access only from the explicit action, emit no success message, and project failure through the existing error surface.
  • [ ] Preserve ordinary table selection, links, resizing, sticky geometry, and Back behavior after copy succeeds or fails.

TE-4.3 — Verify And Transfer

  • [ ] Run focused serializer, resize-state, sticky-offset, control eligibility/dispatch, clipboard failure, lifecycle cleanup, public import-boundary, lint, and whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Manually review pointer and keyboard resizing, Reset, CSV copy into a representative spreadsheet/text editor, long wrapped cells, dark/light themes, representative laptop/desktop widths, Back, and document navigation.
  • [ ] Prove public tables retain the unchanged TE-3 static presentation and load no Manage tool module or control.
  • [ ] Update the durable Content Detail/table presentation owner and Toolbar Model with the shipped Manage extension rule.

Not In Scope

  • a second table view or Manage-specific table renderer;
  • Download CSV, other export formats, file pickers, or server-side export;
  • public promotion of resizing or Copy as CSV;
  • persisted widths, stable table IDs, saved presets, or cross-session settings;
  • freezing more than the first column or user-selected frozen columns;
  • sorting, filtering, grouping, row selection/actions, editing, formulas, charts, or virtualization;
  • parsing Markdown source to recover links or formatting; or
  • diagram presentation, which belongs to TE-5.

The Table Enhancements feature owns sequencing. Content Detail View Concept And Architecture owns the shared view and static-source boundaries.
